records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: a new message: God speaks to Jeremiah from verse 2 to the end of verse 18
decisions.reason: The opening formula starts a fresh word from God. What follows is spoken to Jeremiah himself, about his own life (verses 2-9), and then about what he is to tell the people (verses 10-18). Verses 19-21 are a prayer of Jeremiah and God's reply, set as poetry.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); The word of the LORD came to me: (B); The LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula throughout Jeremiah.

records.heading: Jeremiah is not to marry

records.source: לֹֽא־תִקַּ֥ח לְךָ֖ אִשָּׁ֑ה וְלֹֽא־יִהְי֤וּ לְךָ֙ בָּנִ֣ים וּבָנ֔וֹת בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Not you shall take for yourself [a] wife, and not shall be to you sons and daughters in the place this.
pieces: "Do not marry, and do not have sons or daughters in this place.

L.2: "You shall not take a wife for yourself, and you shall not have sons and daughters in this place.

R.2: "Do not get married, and do not have any sons or daughters here in this place.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah is to stay unmarried and childless: his own life becomes a sign of the coming disaster
decisions.reason: In Israel a man was expected to marry and raise children; to have none was a grief and a loss for the family line. God asks Jeremiah to give this up so that his life shows what is coming: families in this land will not survive (verses 3-4). The prophets sometimes taught by what they did as well as by what they said (13:1-11; Isaiah 8:18; Ezekiel 24:15-24).

decisions.choice: this place: Judah and Jerusalem, the land facing judgment
decisions.reason: "This place" in Jeremiah is often Jerusalem with its temple (7:3, 7; 14:13), and verse 3 widens it to "this land".

decisions.choice: Do not marry / Do not get married
decisions.reason: "Take a wife for yourself" is the Hebrew way of saying "marry". Literal keeps the wording.

records.source: כִּי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַל־הַבָּנִים֙ וְעַל־הַבָּנ֔וֹת הַיִּלּוֹדִ֖ים בַּמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְעַֽל־אִמֹּתָ֞ם הַיֹּלְד֣וֹת אוֹתָ֗ם וְעַל־אֲבוֹתָ֛ם הַמּוֹלִדִ֥ים אוֹתָ֖ם בָּאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh concerning the sons and concerning the daughters, the [ones] born in the place this, and concerning their mothers, the [ones] bearing them, and concerning their fathers, the [ones] begetting them in the land this:
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this about the sons and daughters who are born in this place, about the mothers who give birth to them, and about the fathers who bring them into the world in this land:

L.3: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning the sons and concerning the daughters who are born in this place, and concerning their mothers who bear them, and concerning their fathers who father them in this land:

R.3: Here is the reason. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about the children who are born in this land, and about their mothers and fathers:

decisions.choice: for: verses 3-4 give the reason for the command in verse 2
decisions.reason: Jeremiah is not to raise children because the children born here, and their parents with them, are going to die.

decisions.choice: the mothers who bear them and the fathers who father them: the whole family, parents and children
decisions.reason: The two verbs name what each parent does in bringing a child into the world. Together with "sons and daughters" they take in every household in the land.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (L); the LORD says this (B); This is what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula throughout Isaiah and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: Here is the reason; the children ... their mothers and fathers
decisions.reason: Readable puts the link word "for" as a short sentence of its own, says "children" for "sons and daughters", and joins the mothers and fathers in one phrase.

records.source: מְמוֹתֵ֨י תַחֲלֻאִ֜ים יָמֻ֗תוּ לֹ֤א יִסָּֽפְדוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִקָּבֵ֔רוּ לְדֹ֛מֶן עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה יִֽהְי֑וּ וּבַחֶ֤רֶב וּבָֽרָעָב֙ יִכְל֔וּ וְהָיְתָ֤ה נִבְלָתָם֙ לְמַאֲכָ֔ל לְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּלְבֶהֱמַ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס
records.gloss: [By] deaths of diseases they will die; not they will be mourned and not they will be buried; as dung on [the] face of the ground they will be; and by sword and by famine they will be finished, and will be their corpse[s] as food for [the] birds of the heavens and for [the] beasts of the earth.
pieces: They will die of wasting diseases. No one will mourn them or bury them; they will lie like dung on the surface of the ground. Sword and famine will finish them off, and their dead bodies will become food for the birds of the sky and for the wild animals.

L.4: They will die deaths of diseases; they will not be mourned and they will not be buried; they will be like dung on the face of the ground. And by sword and by famine they will come to an end, and their corpses will be food for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth.

R.4: They will die of terrible diseases. No one will weep for them or bury them. Their bodies will lie on the ground like manure. War and famine will kill them, and the birds and the wild animals will eat their dead bodies.

decisions.choice: deaths of diseases: death from wasting illness
decisions.reason: The second word comes from a verb meaning "to be sick". The same phrase is used of diseases that bring a slow death (2 Chronicles 21:19). Disease and hunger went with every siege.

decisions.choice: unmourned, unburied, like dung on the ground: the worst disgrace for the dead
decisions.reason: To lie unburied was a curse (Deuteronomy 28:26). Jeremiah uses the same picture of dung on the ground in 8:2 and 9:21, and the birds and beasts eating the dead in 7:33; compare 2 Kings 9:37.

decisions.choice: sword and famine: death in war and from hunger
decisions.reason: These two, often with pestilence, are the disasters of war and siege in Jeremiah (14:12, 15-16).

decisions.choice: manure; war
decisions.reason: Readable says "manure" for dung and "war" for the sword, as the Jeremiah terms list has "war, famine and disease" for the fuller list.

records.source: כִּֽי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־תָּבוֹא֙ בֵּ֣ית מַרְזֵ֔חַ וְאַל־תֵּלֵ֣ךְ לִסְפּ֔וֹד וְאַל־תָּנֹ֖ד לָהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אָסַ֨פְתִּי אֶת־שְׁלוֹמִ֜י מֵאֵ֨ת הָעָ֤ם־הַזֶּה֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־הַחֶ֖סֶד וְאֶת־הָֽרַחֲמִֽים׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh: Not you shall enter [a] house of mourning-feast, and not you shall go to lament, and not you shall show sympathy to them; for I have taken away my peace from with the people this, declares Yahweh, the loyal love and the compassion.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Do not go into a house where a funeral meal is being held. Do not go there to mourn or to show them sympathy, for I have withdrawn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} peace from this people, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} loyal love and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} compassion.

L.5: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Do not enter a house of mourning feast, and do not go to lament, and do not show sympathy to them; for I have taken away {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} peace from this people, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the loyal love and the compassion.

R.5: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Do not go into a house where people are sharing a meal to mourn the dead. Do not go there to weep, or to comfort the family. I have taken away {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} peace from these people, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I have taken away {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful love and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mercy.

decisions.choice: a house of mourning feast: a home where a gathering met to share a meal for the dead
decisions.reason: The word (marzeach) names a group that met for a shared meal with drinking. In Amos 6:7 it is a banquet of the rich; here the setting is grief, so it is the meal held with the family of the dead. Verse 7 describes what went on there: bread broken and a cup given to comfort the mourners. The exact nature of the gathering is known only in outline.

decisions.choice: show sympathy: share someone's grief and comfort them
decisions.reason: The verb means to sway or shake the head, a gesture of sorrow made with someone who mourns (15:5; Job 2:11; 42:11).

decisions.choice: God's peace, his loyal love and his compassion are taken away from the people
decisions.reason: Peace (shalom) is well-being in every part of life, given by God. Loyal love (hesed) is his faithfulness to his covenant people, and compassion his tender care for them. All three are the blessings of the covenant; God withdraws them, and so Jeremiah is not to offer comfort either.

decisions.choice: the loyal love and the compassion: further objects of "I have taken away"
decisions.reason: The two nouns stand after "declares the LORD" but belong with "my peace": all three are what God has taken away.

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for hesed in Isaiah and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: a house where a funeral meal is being held / where people are sharing a meal to mourn the dead; my loyal love and my compassion
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain what kind of house is meant, and repeat "my" so the last two nouns clearly go with "taken away". Readable says "mercy" for compassion and repeats the verb.

records.source: וּמֵ֨תוּ גְדֹלִ֧ים וּקְטַנִּ֛ים בָּאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את לֹ֣א יִקָּבֵ֑רוּ וְלֹֽא־יִסְפְּד֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם וְלֹ֣א יִתְגֹּדַ֔ד וְלֹ֥א יִקָּרֵ֖חַ לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And will die great [ones] and small [ones] in the land this; not they will be buried, and not they will lament for them, and not [one] will cut himself and not [one] will make himself bald for them.
pieces: Great and small alike will die in this land. They will not be buried, no one will mourn for them, and no one will gash their body or shave their head for them.

L.6: And great and small will die in this land; they will not be buried, and they will not lament for them, and no one will cut [the body] and no one will shave [the head] bald for them.

R.6: Important people and ordinary people will die in this land. No one will bury them or mourn for them. No one will cut their skin or shave their head to show sorrow for them.

decisions.choice: great and small: everyone, of every rank
decisions.reason: The pair takes in all the people, from leaders to the poorest (6:13; 8:10).

decisions.choice: cutting oneself and shaving the head: signs of grief for the dead
decisions.reason: Gashing the body and shaving part of the head were mourning customs among Israel's neighbors. The law forbade them to Israel (Leviticus 19:28; Deuteronomy 14:1), but they were still practiced (41:5; 47:5). Here they are named only to say that there will be no mourning of any kind.

decisions.choice: they will not lament ... no one will cut: no one at all will mourn
decisions.reason: The verbs have no named subject; they mean that nobody will do these things.

decisions.choice: [the body], [the head] (L); gash their body, shave their head (B); cut their skin, shave their head to show sorrow (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verbs mean "cut oneself" and "make oneself bald". English needs to say what is cut and shaved. Readable adds why it is done.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־יִפְרְס֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם עַל־אֵ֖בֶל לְנַחֲמ֣וֹ עַל־מֵ֑ת וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁק֤וּ אוֹתָם֙ כּ֣וֹס תַּנְחוּמִ֔ים עַל־אָבִ֖יו וְעַל־אִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And not they will break for them over mourning to comfort him over [the] dead, and not they will give to drink them [a] cup of consolations for his father and for his mother.
pieces: No one will break bread for the mourners to comfort them for the dead, and no one will give them the cup of consolation to drink for a father or a mother.

L.7: And they will not break [bread] for them in mourning, to comfort him for the dead, and they will not give them the cup of consolation to drink for his father or for his mother.

R.7: No one will bring food to comfort people who are mourning for the dead. No one will give them a cup of wine to comfort them when their father or mother has died.

decisions.choice: break for them: the Hebrew as written; "bread" is understood
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "break for them". With one small change of vowels the same letters read "break bread", which a few Hebrew manuscripts and the Greek translation have. Either way the sense is breaking bread for the mourners. This description of the manuscripts is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: bread and the cup of consolation: food and drink brought to mourners by friends
decisions.reason: Neighbors brought a meal to a house in mourning, since the family did not cook (2 Samuel 3:35; Ezekiel 24:17, 22). The cup was a drink given to comfort the grieving, likely wine (Proverbs 31:6).

decisions.choice: him, his father, his mother: each mourner
decisions.reason: The verse moves from "them", all the mourners, to "him", each one who has lost a father or mother.

decisions.choice: the mourners ... them; a father or a mother (B); their father or mother (R)
decisions.reason: English keeps the mourners plural throughout, where the Hebrew turns to each one.

decisions.choice: a cup of wine
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup likely held.

records.source: וּבֵית־מִשְׁתֶּ֥ה לֹא־תָב֖וֹא לָשֶׁ֣בֶת אוֹתָ֑ם לֶאֱכֹ֖ל וְלִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: And [a] house of feasting not you shall enter to sit with them to eat and to drink.
pieces: And do not go into a house where there is feasting, to sit with them and eat and drink.

L.8: And you shall not enter a house of feasting to sit with them, to eat and to drink.

R.8: Do not go into a house where people are having a feast, to sit and eat and drink with them.

decisions.choice: a house of feasting: a home where a feast with drinking is held, such as a wedding
decisions.reason: The word for feast comes from the verb "to drink". It is used of wedding feasts (Judges 14:10) and other celebrations. Verse 9 names the joy of weddings.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah is cut off from the people's joy as well as their grief
decisions.reason: He may not share their mourning (verses 5-7) or their celebrations. His lonely life shows that both sorrow and joy are coming to an end in the land (15:17).

records.source: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֨י מַשְׁבִּ֜ית מִן־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה לְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם וּבִֽימֵיכֶ֑ם ק֤וֹל שָׂשׂוֹן֙ וְק֣וֹל שִׂמְחָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חָתָ֖ן וְק֥וֹל כַּלָּֽה׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: Here I [am] making cease from the place this before your eyes and in your days [the] sound of joy and [the] sound of gladness, [the] voice of bridegroom and [the] voice of bride.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Before your eyes and in your own lifetime, I am going to silence in this place the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bridegroom and bride.

L.9: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am going to make the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, cease from this place, before your eyes and in your days.

R.9: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: While you are still alive, you will see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} end the sounds of joy and happiness in this place. No one will hear the happy voices of a bride and groom at their wedding.

decisions.choice: the sound of joy and gladness, of bridegroom and bride: the same words as 7:34
decisions.reason: The silence of weddings, the most joyful times of town life, means that ordinary life has ended. The words come back in 25:10, and the promise that they will be heard again in 33:11.

decisions.choice: your eyes, your days: the people of Jerusalem, and Jeremiah with them
decisions.reason: "Your" is plural here. God speaks past Jeremiah to the whole generation: the disaster will come in their own lifetime, and they will see it.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts: the LORD who commands the armies of heaven
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 1:9, where the title is explained.

decisions.choice: the wording of 7:34 at each level
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew phrase is rendered the same way each time it returns in Jeremiah. Balanced says "in your own lifetime" for "in your days"; Readable says it as "while you are still alive, you will see".

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּ֤י תַגִּיד֙ לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְאָמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֗יךָ עַל־מֶה֩ דִבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את וּמֶ֤ה עֲוֺנֵ֨נוּ֙ וּמֶ֣ה חַטָּאתֵ֔נוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָ֖אנוּ לַֽיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when you tell to the people this all the words these, and they say to you, Concerning what has spoken Yahweh against us all the evil the great this? And what [is] our iniquity, and what [is] our sin that we have sinned against Yahweh our God?
pieces: When you report all these words to this people, they will ask you, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} announced this whole great disaster against us? What is our guilt, and what sin have we committed against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God?'

L.10: And it will be, when you tell this people all these words and they say to you, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken against us all this great evil? And what [is] our iniquity, and what [is] our sin that we have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God?'

R.10: When you tell these people all this, they will ask you, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said that all these terrible things will happen to us? What wrong have we done? What sin have we committed against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God?'

decisions.choice: this great evil: this great disaster
decisions.reason: The word can mean moral evil or harm that comes on someone. Here it is the disaster God has announced, as in Isaiah 45:7.

decisions.choice: the questions protest innocence: the people do not see what they have done wrong
decisions.reason: The same pattern of question and answer is found in 5:19 and 13:22, and in Deuteronomy 29:23-25 and 1 Kings 9:8-9. The answer follows in verses 11-13.

decisions.choice: iniquity and sin: the guilt of wrongdoing and the wrong itself
decisions.reason: The two words are used together for the whole of what the people have done against God.

decisions.choice: spoken ... evil (L); announced ... disaster (B); said ... terrible things will happen (R); iniquity / guilt / wrong
decisions.reason: "Spoken evil against" means announcing disaster. For iniquity Balanced has "guilt", as in Isaiah; Readable says "wrong" because "sin" follows at once.

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם עַל֩ אֲשֶׁר־עָזְב֨וּ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֤ם אוֹתִי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וַיֵּלְכ֗וּ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיַּעַבְד֖וּם וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ לָהֶ֑ם וְאֹתִ֣י עָזָ֔בוּ וְאֶת־תּוֹרָתִ֖י לֹ֥א שָׁמָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: Then you will say to them, Because that forsook your fathers me, declares Yahweh, and they walked after gods other and served them and bowed down to them; and me they forsook, and my law not they kept.
pieces: Then you are to say to them, 'It is because your ancestors abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They followed other gods, served them and bowed down to them. They abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and did not keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction.

L.11: Then you shall say to them, 'Because your fathers forsook {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and went after other gods and served them and bowed down to them; and {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they forsook, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction they did not keep.

R.11: Then tell them, 'It is because your ancestors turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They followed other gods. They served them and worshiped them. They left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and did not obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's answer is God's own word: "declares the LORD" and "me"
decisions.reason: Jeremiah is to answer in God's name, so the answer speaks as God. It runs from here to the end of verse 13.

decisions.choice: forsook: abandoned the LORD, broke faith with him
decisions.reason: The verb is said twice, at the start and near the end of the verse, framing the list of what the fathers did instead (1:16; 2:13; 5:7).

decisions.choice: my instruction (torah): God's teaching for his people
decisions.reason: The word is wider than a code of laws; it is all that God taught Israel to do (2:8; 6:19; 9:12).

decisions.choice: ancestors; instruction (B) / teaching (R)
decisions.reason: "Your fathers" means the earlier generations, men and women, so Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", as 7:26 does. The wording for torah is the one set for Isaiah and Jeremiah.

records.source: וְאַתֶּ֛ם הֲרֵעֹתֶ֥ם לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת מֵאֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְהִנְּכֶ֣ם הֹלְכִ֗ים אִ֚ישׁ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ שְׁרִר֣וּת לִבּֽוֹ־הָרָ֔ע לְבִלְתִּ֖י שְׁמֹ֥עַ אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And you have done evil to act more than your fathers; and here you [are] walking each after [the] stubbornness of his heart, the evil, to not listen to me.
pieces: And you yourselves have behaved even worse than your ancestors. Look, each of you follows the stubbornness of your own evil heart and refuses to listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.12: And you have done more evil than your fathers, and look, you are walking, each one, after the stubbornness of his evil heart, so as not to listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.12: And you have done even worse than your ancestors. Each of you stubbornly follows your own evil heart. You refuse to listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: you have done more evil than your fathers: the present generation is worse still
decisions.reason: The answer turns from the fathers to the people asking the question. They cannot plead that the guilt is all their ancestors' (7:26; compare 31:29-30).

decisions.choice: walking after the stubbornness of his evil heart: following one's own will instead of God's
decisions.reason: A phrase Jeremiah uses again and again (3:17; 7:24; 9:13; 11:8; 13:10).

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of his evil heart (L); the stubbornness of your own evil heart (B); stubbornly follows your own evil heart (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase in Jeremiah, here with "each" and "evil" as the Hebrew has them.

records.source: וְהֵטַלְתִּ֣י אֶתְכֶ֗ם מֵעַל֙ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את עַל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם אַתֶּ֖ם וַאֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם־שָׁ֞ם אֶת־אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֲחֵרִים֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־אֶתֵּ֥ן לָכֶ֖ם חֲנִינָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And I will hurl you from on the land this onto the land that not you have known, you and your fathers; and you will serve there other gods day and night, because not I will give to you favor.
pieces: So I will hurl you out of this land into a land unknown to you and to your ancestors. There you will serve other gods by day and by night, because I will show you no favor.'

L.13: So I will hurl you out of this land into the land that you have not known, you or your fathers, and there you will serve other gods day and night, for I will show you no favor.'

R.13: So I will throw you out of this land into a land that you and your ancestors never knew. There you will serve other gods day and night, and I will not be kind to you.'

decisions.choice: hurl: throw out with force
decisions.reason: The verb is used of throwing a spear (1 Samuel 18:11) and of the king hurled into exile in 22:26, 28.

decisions.choice: you will serve other gods there: they will have what they chose
decisions.reason: Those who served other gods at home will serve them in exile, far from God's land (5:19; Deuteronomy 4:28; 28:36, 64).

decisions.choice: I will show you no favor: God himself withholds his kindness
alternatives: for they will show you no favor (the Greek)
decisions.reason: The verb is "I will give". The Greek translation reads "they will give", making the other gods or the foreign people the ones who show no favor. The Hebrew is followed, and agrees with verse 5. This description of the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: closing single quote
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's answer to the people, begun in verse 11, ends here. God's speech to Jeremiah goes on.

records.source: לָכֵ֛ן הִנֵּֽה־יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־יֵאָמֵ֥ר עוֹד֙ חַי־יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֶעֱלָ֛ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Therefore, look, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, and not it will be said again, [By the] life of Yahweh who brought up the sons of Israel from [the] land of Egypt,
pieces: Therefore, the days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when it will no longer be said, 'As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who brought up the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} from the land of Egypt,'

L.14: Therefore, look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when it will no longer be said, '[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who brought up the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from the land of Egypt,'

R.14: So a time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when people will no longer make a promise by saying, 'As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, the God who led the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of Egypt.'

decisions.choice: therefore: the hope that follows grows out of the judgment
decisions.reason: The word usually draws a conclusion. Here it links the coming return to the scattering just announced: because God will drive the people out, a day will come when he brings them back. It can also be read as "but yet", turning from judgment to hope.

decisions.choice: as the LORD lives: the form of an oath
decisions.reason: An Israelite swore by the life of the LORD (4:2; 5:2; 12:16). The words that follow name him by his greatest act: bringing Israel out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: a new exodus that will outshine the first
decisions.reason: The return from exile will be so great that people will name God by it instead of by the exodus from Egypt (Isaiah 43:16-19). Verses 14-15 come back almost word for word in 23:7-8.

decisions.choice: [As] the LORD lives (L); As surely as the LORD lives (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording used for this oath in 12:16 and in Samuel. Readable adds that saying it is making a promise, as 12:16 does.

decisions.choice: So a time is coming
decisions.reason: Readable says "a time is coming" for "days are coming".

records.heading: Brought back from the north

records.source: כִּ֣י אִם־חַי־יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶעֱלָ֜ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן וּמִכֹּל֙ הָֽאֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִדִּיחָ֖ם שָׁ֑מָּה וַהֲשִֽׁבֹתִים֙ עַל־אַדְמָתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לַאֲבוֹתָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: but rather, [By the] life of Yahweh who brought up the sons of Israel from [the] land of [the] north and from all the lands where he had driven them there; and I will bring them back to their land that I gave to their fathers.
pieces: but, 'As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who brought up the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} from the land of the north and from all the lands where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had driven them.' I will bring them back to their own land, which I gave to their ancestors.

L.15: but, '[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who brought up the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had driven them.' And I will bring them back to their land that I gave to their fathers.

R.15: Instead they will say, 'As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, the God who led the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of the land in the north and out of all the countries where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had scattered them.' I will bring them back to their own land, the land I gave to their ancestors.

decisions.choice: the land of the north: Babylon, the land of exile
decisions.reason: Invaders came on Judah from the north (1:14; 4:6; 6:22), since the road from Babylon ran round by the north. The exiles were taken away by the same road.

decisions.choice: he had driven them ... I will bring them back: the oath speaks of God, then God speaks
decisions.reason: Inside the oath God is named in the third person. After it God speaks for himself again and promises the return.

decisions.choice: the land I gave to their fathers: the promise to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: God swore to give the land to the patriarchs' descendants (7:7; 11:5; Deuteronomy 1:8). The return renews that gift.

decisions.choice: driven (L, B); scattered (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to drive away, to banish. Readable says "scattered", a plainer word for the same thing.

decisions.choice: Instead they will say
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the verb from verse 14 because its verse 14 ends a sentence. In both verses Readable says "the God who led" so that the oath clearly names the LORD by what he did.

records.source: הִנְנִ֨י שֹׁלֵ֜חַ לְדַיָּגִ֥ים רַבִּ֛ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה וְדִיג֑וּם וְאַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן אֶשְׁלַח֙ לְרַבִּ֣ים צַיָּדִ֔ים וְצָד֞וּם מֵעַ֤ל כָּל־הַר֙ וּמֵעַ֣ל כָּל־גִּבְעָ֔ה וּמִנְּקִיקֵ֖י הַסְּלָעִֽים׃
records.gloss: Here I [am] sending for many fishermen, declares Yahweh, and they will fish them; and after so I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them from on every mountain and from on every hill and from [the] clefts of the rocks.
pieces: Look, I am about to summon many fishermen, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they will catch them. Then afterward I will summon many hunters, and they will hunt them down from every mountain, every hill and the cracks in the rocks.

L.16: Look, I am sending for many fishermen, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they will fish for them; and after that I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them from every mountain and from every hill and from the clefts of the rocks.

R.16: Look, I am going to send for many fishermen, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they will catch these people like fish. After that I will send for many hunters. They will hunt them down on every mountain and hill and in the cracks of the rocks.

decisions.choice: fishermen: the form the scribes' margin says to read
decisions.reason: The written letters and the margin give two spellings of the same word; both mean "fishermen".

decisions.choice: the fishermen and hunters are enemies sent to catch the people for judgment
alternatives: God's gathering of his scattered people for the return
decisions.reason: Verses 17-18 speak of judgment, and the prophets picture conquerors catching people like fish (Amos 4:2; Habakkuk 1:14-17). Some read the verse with verse 15, as God gathering his people from every place for the return. The judgment reading is followed.

decisions.choice: every mountain, every hill, the clefts of the rocks: no hiding place anywhere
decisions.reason: People fled to the hills and hid in caves and cracks of the rock (Isaiah 2:19, 21; Amos 9:1-3). None of it will hide them.

decisions.choice: catch these people like fish
decisions.reason: Readable says that the fishing is a picture, and that the people are what is caught.

records.source: כִּ֤י עֵינַי֙ עַל־כָּל־דַּרְכֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א נִסְתְּר֖וּ מִלְּפָנָ֑י וְלֹֽא־נִצְפַּ֥ן עֲוֺנָ֖ם מִנֶּ֥גֶד עֵינָֽי׃
records.gloss: For my eyes [are] on all their ways; not they are hidden from before me, and not is concealed their iniquity from before my eyes.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes are on every path they take. They are not hidden from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and their guilt is not concealed from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight.

L.17: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes are on all their ways; they are not hidden from before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and their iniquity is not concealed from before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes.

R.17: I see everything they do. Nothing they do is hidden from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Their sin cannot be kept out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight.

decisions.choice: my eyes are on all their ways: I see all that they do
decisions.reason: "Ways" are a person's conduct, the paths they take in life (32:19). God's eyes on them here means that he sees, so that none can escape (verse 16).

decisions.choice: iniquity: the guilt of their wrongdoing
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sin (R); sight (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Isaiah. Readable says "I see everything they do" for "my eyes are on all their ways".

records.source: וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֣י רִֽאשׁוֹנָ֗ה מִשְׁנֵ֤ה עֲוֺנָם֙ וְחַטָּאתָ֔ם עַ֖ל חַלְּלָ֣ם אֶת־אַרְצִ֑י בְּנִבְלַ֤ת שִׁקּֽוּצֵיהֶם֙ וְתוֹעֲב֣וֹתֵיהֶ֔ם מָלְא֖וּ אֶת־נַחֲלָתִֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And I will repay first [the] double of their iniquity and their sin, because they profaned my land with [the] corpse[s] of their detestable things, and [with] their abominations they have filled my inheritance.
pieces: First I will repay them double for their guilt and their sin, because they have defiled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land with the lifeless corpses of their detestable idols and filled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance with their abominations."

L.18: And I will repay first the double of their iniquity and their sin, because they have defiled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land with the corpses of their detestable things, and with their abominations they have filled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance."

R.18: But first I will pay them back twice over for their sin and guilt. They have made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land unclean with their dead, worthless idols. They have filled the land that belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with things I hate."

decisions.choice: first: before the return of verses 14-15
decisions.reason: The judgment comes first, and only then the new exodus. The word is missing in the Greek translation, which some take to mean it was added to tie the two passages together. This description of the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: double: a full repayment
decisions.reason: The word means "double" or "a second portion". It may stress that the penalty is full, the equal of the wrong, rather than twice as much (17:18; Isaiah 40:2).

decisions.choice: the corpses of their detestable things: idols, lifeless as dead bodies
decisions.reason: The idols are called corpses because they have no life (Leviticus 26:30). Corpses also made a place unclean (Numbers 19:11-16), so the picture fits the defiling of the land.

decisions.choice: my land, my inheritance: the land as God's own possession
decisions.reason: The same complaint as 2:7: the people defiled God's land and made his inheritance detestable.

decisions.choice: detestable idols, abominations (B); dead, worthless idols, things I hate (R)
decisions.reason: "Detestable things" in the prophets are idols. Readable explains both words.

decisions.choice: closing double quote
decisions.reason: God's speech to Jeremiah, begun in verse 2, ends here.

records.source: יְהוָ֞ה עֻזִּ֧י וּמָעֻזִּ֛י וּמְנוּסִ֖י בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה אֵלֶ֗יךָ גּוֹיִ֤ם יָבֹ֨אוּ֙ מֵֽאַפְסֵי־אָ֔רֶץ וְיֹאמְר֗וּ אַךְ־שֶׁ֨קֶר֙ נָחֲל֣וּ אֲבוֹתֵ֔ינוּ הֶ֖בֶל וְאֵֽין־בָּ֥ם מוֹעִֽיל׃
records.gloss: Yahweh, my strength and my stronghold and my refuge in [the] day of distress, to you nations will come from [the] ends of [the] earth, and they will say, Surely lies inherited our fathers, futility, and there is not in them [one] profiting.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my strength, my fortress, my refuge on the day of trouble, \q to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the nations will come from the ends of the earth \q and say, "Our ancestors inherited nothing but lies, \q worthless idols that did them no good at all."

L.19: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my strength and my stronghold, and my refuge in the day of distress, \q to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} nations will come from the ends of the earth \q and will say, "Surely our fathers inherited lies, \q worthlessness, and there is nothing in them that profits."

R.19: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make me strong and keep me safe. You are my shelter when trouble comes. \q Nations will come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} from the farthest parts of the earth. \q They will say, "Our ancestors had nothing but false gods. \q Those idols were worthless and could not help them at all."

decisions.choice: Jeremiah turns to God in a prayer of trust
decisions.reason: God's speech has ended. Jeremiah speaks to the LORD in poetry, as in his laments (15:10-21), but here with confidence: the LORD is his strength and refuge. God answers in verse 21.

decisions.choice: the nations will come to the LORD from the ends of the earth
decisions.reason: While Judah follows idols, Jeremiah looks ahead to the day when the nations themselves will turn from their idols to the LORD (3:17; 4:2; 12:16; Isaiah 2:2-4).

decisions.choice: lies, worthlessness, nothing that profits: idols
decisions.reason: "Lies" are false gods (10:14). The word for worthlessness means breath or vapor, something with nothing in it (2:5; 8:19; 10:8, 15). "Nothing that profits" echoes 2:8, 11.

decisions.choice: surely: "only", "nothing but"
decisions.reason: The small word stresses that lies were all the fathers received.

decisions.choice: you make me strong and keep me safe; my shelter; false gods; those idols
decisions.reason: Readable turns the three titles into short clauses, and says plainly that the lies and the worthless things are idols.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

records.heading: The nations will come

records.source: הֲיַעֲשֶׂה־לּ֥וֹ אָדָ֖ם אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְהֵ֖מָּה לֹ֥א אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: ? Will make for himself a human gods? And they [are] not gods.
pieces: Can people make gods for themselves? \q Such things are not gods at all!

L.20: Will a human make gods for himself? \q And they [are] not gods!

R.20: Can people make their own gods? \q No! The things they make are not gods at all.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: Something a human makes cannot be a god (2:11; 5:7; 10:3-5; Isaiah 44:9-20). The verse may still be the nations speaking, or Jeremiah's own comment on their words; it means the same either way.

decisions.choice: a human: any person, a mortal
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being, set against God.

decisions.choice: people ... themselves
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "people" for the single "human", since the question is about anyone.

records.source: לָכֵן֙ הִנְנִ֣י מֽוֹדִיעָ֔ם בַּפַּ֣עַם הַזֹּ֔את אוֹדִיעֵ֥ם אֶת־יָדִ֖י וְאֶת־גְּבֽוּרָתִ֑י וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־שְׁמִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Therefore, here I [am] making them know at the time this; I will make them know my hand and my might, and they will know that my name [is] Yahweh.
pieces: Therefore I am going to teach them; \q this time I will make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} might known to them, \q and they will know that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: Therefore, look, I am going to make them know; \q this time I will make them know {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} might, \q and they will know that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: So I will teach them. \q This time I will show them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} strength. \q Then they will know that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: God answers; "them" may be the nations or Judah
decisions.reason: God speaks again in the first person. "Them" may be the nations who make idols (verses 19-20), or the people of Judah, who will learn through judgment who God is (verses 10-18).

decisions.choice: my hand and my might: my power in action
decisions.reason: The hand stands for strength put to work, as in the exodus (Exodus 13:9; Deuteronomy 26:8).

decisions.choice: they will know that my name is Yahweh: they will know God as he truly is
decisions.reason: The name stands for who God is. The words echo the exodus, when God acted so that Israel and Egypt would know that he is the LORD (Exodus 6:3, 7; 7:5; compare Isaiah 42:8).

decisions.choice: teach them; power for "hand"
decisions.reason: The verb means "make them know"; Balanced and Readable say "teach" for the first and keep "make ... known" (B) or "show" (R) for the second. "Hand" means power.
